title: Rolling sample delta cache window for embedding deduplication and low-latency rerank
creator: Marco Chen
description: Problem: Reranking endpoints and embedding pipelines show high tail latency and wasted upstream compute due to many near-duplicate prefix inputs (common headers, doc boilerplate, repeated context sequences). Current cache logic dedupes whole-sequence keys and applies a single TTL per tenant or prefix cohort, which misses opportunities to reuse partial prefix embeddings and to gracefully expire transient spikes. This ticket proposes a novel 'rolling sample delta cache window' (RSDCW) that stores compact delta-encoded prefix embeddings sampled across a short rolling window, with probabilistic tombstones and micro-cohort TTLs to reduce stale collisions and improve hit rate for rerank workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Server-side embedding cache implements rolling sample delta window: stores base fingerprint + compact deltas for up to N recent suffixes per prefix fingerprint
End-to-end latency for rerank (median and p95) improves by >=10% median and >=5% p95 on benchmark workloads compared to baseline
Cache hit rate for rerank workloads increases by >=18% on internal query replay dataset (tenant-weighted)
No correctness regressions: rerank output rank-order preserves top-3 for >=99.5% of queries compared to cold compute baseline
Graceful rollout plan and automatic rollback triggers are implemented (error rate spike >0.5% or latency p95 increase >15%)
Logging, dashboards, and alerts for per-tenant hit-rate, eviction churn, tombstone count, and version-mismatch rate added to Console
implementation_notes: Cache key format: v2|tenant_cohort|prefix_shingle_hash|window_sequence_id — include model_version tag to avoid cross-version reuse
Storage: delta-encode contiguous KV-cache entries using compact float16 deltas for embedding vectors; fall back to full-vector store for cold items to simplify reads
TTL strategy: micro-cohort TTLs derived from query inter-arrival distributions (short-lived cohorts: 30s, medium: 5m, long: 1h); allow tenant overrides via Dedicated plan config
Probabilistic tombstones: write lightweight tombstone markers for content-hash collisions with decaying TTL to prevent immediate re-inserts from noisy sources
Consistency during model rollouts: maintain dual-read for a short period (read latest model_vector first, if miss check previous-model namespace) and schedule background rehydration
Eviction policy: LRFU-style hybrid that favors recently-accessed prefixes and penalizes high-write churn prefixes to reduce thrash
Read path: try exact prefix delta sequence, then attempt prefix-subsequence merge (coalesce deltas) before fallback to compute; add fast path for 'short-circuit' hits used by top-k rerankers
Instrumentation: sample-on-hit payloads (1/1000) to verify reconstructed vector fidelity; track bytes_saved_per_hit and compute_saved_ms per tenant
Rollout: feature-flagged, will enable for 5% of production rerank traffic first, then 25%, 50%, 100% with automated checks
Backwards compatibility: expose opt-out header for customers that require strict determinism
rollout_plan: Canary at 5% traffic to 'rerank' route for low-volume tenants for 48 hours
Observe hit rate, eviction churn, latency spread. If thresholds met, expand to 25% for 72 hours
Run an A/B quality check on rerank relevance using holdout evaluation prompts (compare top-k overlap and MRR) during each stage
Full rollout contingent on <0.5% error increase and >=10% median latency improvement across cohorts
If rollback required, automatically disable delta reads and revert to base cache namespace while preserving collected telemetry
benchmarks_and_findings: Local load tests (synthetic replay of 10M queries): preliminary prototype shows median latency improvement of 12% and p95 improvement of 6% on rerank-only path
Hit-rate uplift varies by tenant: heavy-chat tenants see +24% hit rate, document-indexing tenants see +9% (higher diversity)
Memory overhead for delta indices measured at +6% in hot shards; expected amortization by compute saved
Reconstruction fidelity: mean cosine similarity of reconstructed vs. full-vector = 0.9991 for tested models (1B and 3B families)
Worst-case behavior: pathological churn workloads can cause temporary tombstone accumulation — mitigation via write-rate dampening and surge TTL shortening
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Model update incompatibility — Mitigation: always include model_version in key and run dual-read during rollouts
Risk: Increased memory usage on hot shards — Mitigation: throttle delta creation under memory pressure and prefer full-vector cold-store
Risk: Incorrect rerank ordering due to delta quantization — Mitigation: conservative quantization settings and fidelity sampling checks; fall back to exact compute for top-k critical flows
Risk: Tenant privacy/side-channel via shared cache keys — Mitigation: tenant_cohort namespacing and optional tenant-isolated cache for Dedicated customers
